text: The glass kiln has heated the sand. Adding coal can maintain slow melting, while connecting power can greatly increase output.
The newly opened workshops are all drawing power from the same cable. Another public power station is needed.
The public power station is now staffed. Each electrician adds coal to tend the generator and can supply ten units of immediate power steadily to the grid.
The new furnaces have large appetites, and the ore supply is gradually falling behind. The old mine still needs reinforced pit timber and widened haulage tunnels.
Mine support expansion is complete, adding eight mining stations underground.
After adding blowers and a hoist, the depths of the coal kiln can accommodate more miners.
Coal-zone ventilation expansion is complete, adding eight coal-mining stations underground.
The chemical engineer has drawn up spray absorption and filtration pipelines. Filtering the furnace smoke also requires power and spare parts.
The work area's purification facilities have been connected to the flue. Each cycle expends power, chemicals, wood, and parts to wash toxic dust out of the dense smoke.
Basic Chemicals
Screening, acid washing, and purification have been set into reproducible procedures. Crude ore has been turned into the first batch of basic chemicals in coal-fired furnaces.
Steelmaking
The trial steel bars showed no cracking under the heavy hammer. Steelmakers can continue exploring furnace temperatures and mixtures.

Precision Machine Tool

The vernier calipers, carbide turning tools, and lead screw test pieces all meet tolerance requirements. A precision machine shop can be built under the "Processing" category in a district; once complete, assign precision machinists on the Hearth City page. The lathe must not lose power while running.
Basic Electronics Processes

Stable manual procedures have been established for insulated packaging, solder joints, and control circuits. An electronics assembly room can be built under the "Processing" category in a district or municipal government; components still require on-duty workers to expend materials and power to produce them.
